newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures edge up, seen building base.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures edge up, seen building base.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ambled higher in slow Thursday morning trade as the market tried to consolidate its recent sharp gains.
"We see a consolidation at the moment," said one trader. The explosive rally in New York arabica futures also lost some steam on Wednesday with the market now seen taking a much-needed breather.
Others said there's more room on the upside in London.
"It's forming a base," said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst. "If the base is a real one, it could go a lot higher. It's overbought, but I don't think that matters a lot."
Bucking lower pre-opening expectations, benchmark July gapped $6 up at the open and rose further to an intraday high of $1,887, a new one-year high.
It then dipped into the minus column before finishing the morning business just $5 up at $1,875.
The second-month position had jumped by 23 percent to $1,887 since the March 25 low of $1,535 as the market continued its sharp upswing that started in early January.
Traders and analysts were now looking at $1,900 as a pyschological target, with $1,930 as the next real hurdle.
"The funds ain't long and roasters are not fully covered either," said one trader. "Furthermore, New York's got further to go on the upside."
Overall volume in London was a scant 2,344 lots.
Activity in New York is expected to slow on Thursday ahead of the key U.S. green stock data due after market closes.

Expectations are for a slight increase of between 100,000 to 300,000 bags but broker GNI said a large proportion of any increase could be from robusta coffee, which would not necessarily be bearish for arabicas.
After the midday pause, German statistician F.O. Licht revised upwards its 1996/97 world coffee crop forecast to 97.6 million bags from its November estimate of 96.45 million.
The revision reflected an increase in robusta production.
But Licht said the consumer stock position would remain highly precarious as initial consumption forecasts suggests there would be little if any improvement to inventories.

LIFFE certified coffee stocks rose to 4,858 five-tonne lots in April from 4,008 in March. Traders said the increase was slightly below their expectations. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 5424985
